title: Locally representable fppf sheaves and scheme descent data
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with the site and all families in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(W,Z)$ for a $T$-scheme $Z$. All fibre products are over $T$ unless another base is specified [def-pc-fibre-product]. A scheme descent datum on this covering consists of $T_i$-schemes $X_i$ and isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:X_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TX_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$, whose pullbacks to triple overlaps satisfy $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$. It is effective if there is a $T$-scheme $X$ with isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$ inducing the given $\phi_{ij}$; this is the covering-family form of [def-pd-descent-datum]. There is an equivalence between the category of scheme descent data on this covering and the category of sheaves of sets $H$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that each $h_{T_i}\times H$ is represented by a scheme. Under this equivalence the schemes representing $h_{T_i}\times H$ are the $X_i$, their comparison isomorphisms on overlaps give the descent datum, and $H$ is representable by a $T$-scheme if and only if the corresponding descent datum is effective.

source.place: Tag 02W5, lemma-descent-data-sheaves, specialization to the fppf topology, including clauses (1) and (2).

proof.text: Use Mathlib’s subcanonicity of the fppf topology and its induced slice topology: representable functors of points, with the required universe lift, are sheaves. Generate the covering sieve from the fppf precoverage. The fully faithful part of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] says restriction of global sheaves to this covering is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 02W5, lemma-descent-data-sheaves and following remark; categorical quasi-inverse and effectivity checks.

proof.text: Take G and its natural descent-datum comparison from [lem-trf-fppf-scheme-data-sheaf-gluing]. The forgetful functor from [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum] is fully faithful by the induced-category definition. Hence G is fully faithful, since its composite with restriction is isomorphic to that forgetful functor. For a locally representable sheaf H, choose its representing object on each slice and package these with the canonical sheaf descent datum as R(H). The comparison for R(H) lifts uniquely through fully faithful restriction to an isomorphism G(R(H)) ≅ H. Thus G is essentially surjective and gives the required equivalence. Its local product representations and natural comparison are exactly those supplied by the gluing theorem.

source.place: Tag 02W5, lemma-descent-data-sheaves and following remark; categorical quasi-inverse and effectivity checks.

proof.text: If H is represented by X, the map/pullback adjunction on slices represents its restriction by X ×_T U_i [def-pc-fibre-product]. Uniqueness of representing objects [lem-pc-representable-unique] identifies each specified local scheme with this pullback. Compose this identification with the first projection to obtain q_i and its Cartesian square. Naturality of inverse representing bijections and the given descent-datum comparison show that all transition maps preserve q_i. This is exactly geometric effectivity in [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum].

source.place: Tag 02W5, lemma-descent-data-sheaves and following remark; categorical quasi-inverse and effectivity checks.

proof.text: Conversely, a geometric realization X and Cartesian maps q_i represent the restriction of h_X on each slice by the specified local schemes. Compose representing isomorphisms to obtain local isomorphisms from the given datum to the restriction of h_X. The transition invariance in [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum] initially tests identity objects; pullback compatibility of descent transitions and naturality extend it to every object of every overlap slice. Thus these local isomorphisms form an isomorphism of descent data. Since h_X is a sheaf, the fully faithful restriction of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] lifts it to an isomorphism H ≅ h_X. Therefore H is representable.

lean.statement: theorem fppfSheafRepresentabilityDescentData {I : Type (u + 1)} (T : Scheme.{u}) (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T) (hcov : Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T) : ∃ e : SchemeCoverDescent f ≌ (IsLocallyRepresentableFppfSheaf f).FullSubcategory, Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ (IsLocallyRepresentableFppfSheaf f).ι ⋙ (Scheme.fppfTopology.pseudofunctorOver (Type (u + 1))).toDescentData f ≅ schemeCoverDescentForget f) ∧ (∀ (D : SchemeCoverDescent f) (i : I), Nonempty ((Limits.prod (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj (Over.mk (f i))) (e.functor.obj D).obj.obj).RepresentableBy ((Over.map (f i)).obj (D.localScheme i)))) ∧ (∀ D : SchemeCoverDescent f, (e.functor.obj D).obj.obj.IsRepresentable ↔ D.IsEffective)
